text:
I don’t think I’ve ever seen a tweet from this account was anything but an absolute laser

like, violently in agreement

on this one... I would just add 3-4 thoughts, most of which r prob dogshit, but perhaps a single word or phrase somewhere in there helps u see the world a little bit clearer.

the first is that "the weak man attacks others, the strong man attacks himself"

a weak man cannot be hard on himself.

why? bc the interior can't withstand it. something is cracked or broken in there. the Jungian shadow exists in everyone -- u either face it, or u pretend it doesn't exist

there is a base level of intestinal fortitude required for you to be ruthless on yourself

hence why ppl worth studying or emulating, they are constantly destroying and rebuilding themselves. 

u don't see them worrying about or commenting on other people’s flaws or weaknesses. one, there is no time for it, two, there is no benefit

once u realize how difficult it is to change urself, u laugh at the futility of trying to change somebody else.

so u can usually read ppl pretty fast, based on how much time they spend gossiping about others. rather than take my word for it, think of 10 people u admire and respect on here, and then scroll their feed

alternate angle, think of a strong mind (ie Munger) constantly destroying itself, vs a weak mind glued to long held priors

last...there's deeper layers to this, although I can't yet supply the right words for it. I'm thinking of a phrase from Leopardi - "the courage of philosophical pessimism"

not everyone wants to see the world as it really is...its ugly. this is King Solomon's "in much wisdom is much grief," the burden of consciousness...many passages from Schopenhauer, some from Jung, Byron's "sorrow is knowledge, those who know the most mourn the deepest." it all connects.

same principle for the quoted tweet, as for one human, as for human nature, as for the totality of the universe. unfortunately i'm not bright enough to piece it all together for u

until then - "ceterum censeo carthaginem esse delendam."
